submission.justification: Absorber-F1 at 6 mm gave the best simulated resolution: 3.14% at 100 GeV. F1 beat F3 and F2 at every thickness I compared. F1 scan: 2 mm 3.63%, 3 mm 3.39%, 4 mm 3.26%, 5 mm 3.2% (2025 summary), 6 mm 3.14%, 8 mm 3.76%, 10 mm 4.40%. I did not scan F1 at 7 mm. Caveat: I could not verify the hard residual dose requirement (<=20 uSv/h at 1 m after one week). None of the project documents contain activation or dose data, and the simulation tool only returns resolution. F1 is a dense alloy and might fail the limit. Someone must check the dose for F1 before this choice is final. If F1 fails, fall back to F3 at about 4 mm (3.93%), and if F3 fails too, to F2 (5.1% at 5 mm), which is the standard structural absorber.

requirements.requirement: Best possible energy resolution at 100 GeV
requirements.evidence: F1 at 6 mm gives 3.137%, the best of the points simulated. F3 reached 3.93% at 4 mm and F2 5.1% at 5 mm.

requirements.requirement: Residual dose rate at 1 m after one week <= 20 uSv/h (hard)
requirements.evidence: No dose or activation data in any document or simulation output. This needs to be checked for F1 before the choice is final.

requirements.requirement: Material is one of the three candidates
